title: Operating Systems
subject: operating-systems
description: Flip-card revision for operating systems — process scheduling, deadlocks, memory management, and paging for fast C-CAT recall.

cards.front: What does a Process Control Block (PCB) store?
cards.back: Process ID, state, program counter, CPU registers, scheduling info — everything needed for a context switch

cards.front: Which scheduling algorithm risks starving long processes?
cards.back: SJF (Shortest Job First) — short jobs keep jumping the queue ahead of it
Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait — ALL 4 must hold simultaneously

cards.front: What does the Banker's Algorithm do?
cards.back: Deadlock avoidance — checks whether granting a resource request keeps the system in a 'safe state'

cards.front: Key difference between mutex and semaphore
cards.back: A mutex has ownership (only the locking thread can unlock it); a semaphore is a general counter any thread can signal
With FIFO page replacement specifically, adding more frames can sometimes cause MORE page faults, not fewer

cards.front: Paging causes which type of fragmentation?
cards.back: Internal fragmentation (the last page may be only partially filled)

cards.front: Segmentation causes which type of fragmentation?

cards.back: Too many processes competing for too little physical memory — the degree of multiprogramming is too high

cards.front: SCAN disk scheduling is also known as?
cards.back: The Elevator Algorithm — the head moves in one direction, reverses at the end

cards.front: What does the TLB (Translation Lookaside Buffer) cache?
cards.back: Recent page-table lookups, avoiding a full memory access for every address translation
